Dear Nicolas,

Thank you for your patience while our Executive Resolution team
conducted a thorough re-investigation into your bootloader unlocking
request. We appreciate you providing the correct hardware information so
we could ensure your account records are completely accurate.

Our specialized investigation into your Motorola Moto G Play 2024 with
the IMEI ending in 3198 confirms that this specific device has fully
satisfied our legacy carrier compliance thresholds. Our system records
verify that under the legacy Verizon 60-Day Lock Policy tied to your
January 6, 2026 activation, the device successfully completed its
network tenure. On March 6, 2026, under Ticket ID: 1338984705, an
administrative override was successfully completed, permanently
rendering the device Network Unlocked. There are zero active cellular
operator locks or SIM constraints applied to this device by our network.

Regarding your request to remove the firmware restriction causing the

fast boot execution loop: Straight Talk Wireless distributes retail

hardware utilizing standard carrier software profiles provided directly

by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). On these branded models,
the core secure-boot partitions are systematically locked from the

factory by the manufacturer to preserve system integrity.

According to Section Ill, Clause 13 of the binding Straight Talk Terms
and Conditions of Service, consumers explicitly agree "not to unlock,
root, re-flash, jailbreak, tamper with or alter the build state of your
Straight Talk phone." Because this partition restriction is compiled

into the physical hardware's operating system built at the factory

level, Straight Talk Wireless does not possess custom firmware
modifications, backend whitelists, or engineering mechanisms capable of
overriding or rewriting these localized OEM security boundaries.

Thus, because your device has already been granted a complete and
permanent cellular network release, Straight Talk Wireless is unable to
authorize an alternative hardware replacement or implement a technical
firmware modification.

We attempted to contact you today, May 30, 2026, at 2:46 PM EST via your
contact number (I) to discuss these findings; however, our

call was routed to voicemail.

If you have any further questions regarding this policy, please simply

reply to this email. Otherwise, you may reach our specialized team

directly at 1-888-251-8169 (PIN: HMO). Our hours of operation are

Monday through Sunday, 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM EST.

Thank you for your time, and we appreciate your understanding.
